articles.headline: Transfer rumors, news: Juventus eye moves for Šeško, Balogun
articles.description: Juventus are keeping tabs on possible moves for forwards Benjamin Šeško and Folarin Balogun. Transfer Talk has the latest.
articles.body:
Juventus are weighing up approaches for Manchester United striker Benjamin Šeško and AS Monaco forward Folarin Balogun, while Atlético Madrid winger Álex Baena has caught the eye of Arsenal. Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Juventus are weighing up approaches for Manchester United striker Benjamin Šeško and AS Monaco forward Folarin Balogun, with plans to land a striker in January, Calciomercato reports. The Serie A club are keen to acquire a physical front man in the next transfer window, when they are expected to have around €100 million available to reinforce their squad. Šeško, 23, hasn't featured for United since Sept. 16 in the EFL Cup against Brighton & Hove Albion due to injury, while a move for 25-year-old Balogun could be possible after Monaco accepted an initial €40m offer from Everton in the summer before the deal fell through.

- Arsenal are keeping tabs on Atlético Madrid winger Álex Baena, TEAMtalk reports. An offer worth €80 million is expected to be required to secure the 25-year-old's transfer, as the Gunners explore the market for a top option to play on the left flank. The Premier League side could face competition from Bayern Munich for Baena, who has scored five goals and provided three assists in 11 LaLiga matches this season. Arsenal could raise funds for this with the exit of midfielder Martín Zubimendi, amid interest from Real Madrid and Barcelona, according to TEAMtalk. The 27-year-old has struggled to start regularly since the arrival of Bruno Guimarães and the Gunners would want a fee around the €60m that they parted with to land him from Real Sociedad in July 2025.

- Manchester United are considering a move for Al Ahli striker Ivan Toney as they prioritize adding depth at the No. 9 position, according to Football Insider. The Red Devils are monitoring the 30-year-old, who has scored 12 goals in nine Saudi Pro League matches this season, with several other options also on their shortlist. Toney has been in Saudi Arabia since joining Al Ahli from Brentford in the summer of 2024.

- Barcelona are interested in Tottenham Hotspur midfielder Lucas Bergvall, according to Football Insider. Bergvall, 20, chose Spurs over Barcelona in 2024, but the Blaugrana are still monitoring him, though Spurs are in control of his future as his contract is not set to expire until the summer of 2031. The Sweden international has made four Premier League appearances this season and has also emerged on the radar of Napoli.

- Al-Hilal have ended their pursuit of Manchester United midfielder Bruno Fernandes, TalkSPORT reports. The Saudi Pro League club were strongly linked with a move for the 32-year-old over the summer, but they aren't expected to make a new approach for him in January, with no plans to free up any of their overseas player slots. articles.headline: Champions League live updates: Arsenal, Man City in action, Fenerbahçe stun Liverpool
articles.description: Fenerbahçe get a shock win against Liverpool, while Arsenal and Manchester City are both in action as UEFA Champions League league phase continues Wednesday.
articles.body:
The Champions!

The UEFA Champions League continues Wednesday with another action-packed slate of league phase fixtures.

We kick things off with the early matches, in which Liverpool traveled to face Fenerbahçe and it was the hosts that ended up winning 3-2, while Real Madrid took on AEK Athens and Jose Mourinho's side got a last-minute goal to win 3-2.

Later, Manchester City face off against RB Leipzig, while last season's runners-up Arsenal will look to continue their unbeaten European campaign in the Czech capital against Slavia Prague.

Elsewhere, Borussia Dortmund host Real Betis, Porto face off against Napoli and PSV Eindhoven take on Club Brugge. Finally, Lens welcome Como, while Viking face Sabah to round out the day's nine-match slate.

Enjoy all the latest updates, goals, highlights and analysis from across Europe!

articles.headline: Colts' Shane Steichen defends Jonathan Taylor usage, says RB will keep role
articles.description: Jonathan Taylor will continue to play his usual role with the Colts despite being at the center of trade talks with multiple teams, Shane Steichen said.
articles.body:
INDIANAPOLIS -- Indianapolis Colts star running back Jonathan Taylor will continue to play his usual role despite being at the center of trade talks with multiple teams, coach Shane Steichen said Tuesday.

Steichen was pressed about the organization's approach with Taylor, who played 38 snaps in the Colts' 42-7 loss Sunday to the Jacksonville Jaguars.

Steichen said there has been no change to the Colts' plan for Taylor in Week 9 against the Dallas Cowboys.

"There's a lot of stuff out there right now," Steichen said of speculation surrounding Taylor. "He's on our football team and he's excited for this opportunity to go play. He wants to go win this game."

Taylor has attracted trade interest from numerous teams since the Colts (2-6) signaled in recent weeks that they are directing their focus toward the future. The Colts fired general manager Chris Ballard last month and traded highly respected veterans Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner last week.

Relatedly, receiver Josh Downs has requested a trade, though he also played last Sunday and is expected to play against Dallas.

"I'm focused on now," Downs said Wednesday. "We play the Cowboys this week. We have practice today. We're trying to go out there and win. ... I've got to focus on now. That's what's most important."

Steichen acknowledged the Arizona Cardinals' recent decision to hold Marvin Harrison Jr. out of a game after a trade involving the receiver had been agreed to with the Houston Texans. But Steichen said there have been no conversations to that effect between him and the Colts' front office.

"During this time of year, people are going to call," he said. "That's just part of the business. But, again, you've got to be a professional and show up to work."

articles.headline: Late Valverde stunner seals Real Madrid comeback in Athens
articles.description: Federico Valverde netted a stoppage-time winner as Real Madrid beat AEK Athens 3-2 in Greece on Wednesday with another dramatic Champions League comeback.
articles.body:
Federico Valverde netted a stoppage-time winner as Real Madrid beat AEK Athens 3-2 in Greece on Wednesday with another dramatic Champions League comeback.

Aboubakary Koita opened the scoring for the hosts in the 12th minute before Jude Bellingham scored a stylish equaliser 20 minutes later, and Stavros Pilios fired the hosts back in front with 15 minutes remaining in the contest.

Kylian Mbappé drew the sides level less than three minutes later, and it was heartbreak for Athens after Real Madrid captain Valverde completed the turnaround in the second minute of added time.

Madrid's comeback ensured a second successive dramatic away day for Jose Mourinho's side in Europe following their 4-3 success at Roma having trailed 3-1 with seven minutes left.

It was a record-breaking night for Bellingham, who became the youngest player -- at 23 years and 128 days old -- to make 60 appearances in the competition's history, overtaking former Real Madrid goalkeeper Iker Casillas, who was 23 years and 167 days old in 2004.

Bellingham also became the youngest player to score in seven successive Champions League seasons, surpassing Mbappé, who was 23 years and 260 days old when he set the previous record in the 2022-23 season.

The hosts got out to an encouraging start, with several shots on target, before Koita fired them in front.

He was teed up by former Real Madrid forward Luka Jovic and dragged the low pass on to his left foot before powering the ball in between Antonio Rüdiger and Marc Cucurella, and beyond Thibaut Courtois.

Bellingham initially thought he had equalised in the 28th minute from a corner, but the offside flag was raised and the call upheld following a VAR check.

He got his goal four minutes later, and it was a stylish one, a brilliant backheel flick from 12 yards out, teed up perfectly by Cucurella, to draw the sides level.

The unmarked Cucurella could have made it three 10 minutes after the restart, teed up perfectly by Mbappé, but he was unable to lift the ball, allowing Lazaros Rota to slide in for a critical tackle.

Mbappé came close, curling marginally wide just after the hour, then had another effort saved, and was denied a shot with just over 20 minutes remaining by an excellent Pilios tackle.

Pilios sent the stands into raptures with 15 minutes to go in normal time, latching on to Koita's weighted pass and firing home through the legs of Courtois.

But soon after Mbappé burst in and met Denzel Dumfries' ball across goal to equalise, then drew an excellent Alberto Brignoli save with less than five minutes remaining in normal time.

Valverde then ensured the visitors maintained their flawless record in the competition with a slick finish from the edge of the box into the top corner.

Koita, who was seen protesting after the final whistle, was shown a red card by the officials.

Information from PA was used in this recap.

articles.headline: Greenwood leads Fenerbahce rally to end Liverpool's perfect UCL start
articles.description: Even Liverpool 's multi-million pound bench could not rescue a team floundering in Istanbul as a chaotic performance was punished by Fenerbahce as they twice came from behind to win 3-2.
articles.body:
Even Liverpool's multi-million pound bench could not rescue a team floundering in Istanbul as a chaotic performance was punished by Fenerbahce as they twice came from behind to win 3-2.

Alexander Isak had scored within three minutes of coming on to put the visitors ahead going into the final quarter but, like in the first half, the lead lasted just four minutes before former West Brom trainee Archie Brown equalised courtesy of some lax defending.

But worse was to follow as Vedat Muriqi outjumped three players to nod in the winner and end Liverpool's 100% record.

And while manager Andoni Iraola will be scrutinised for making five changes, including resting three of his front four in Sunday's defeat to Arsenal, it was the way the team lost their cool and control in a game they had in hand which was more damaging.

It was a harsh result on 19-year-old Trey Nyoni, who belied his relative inexperience with a composed performance capped by an excellent volley to open the scoring, becoming Liverpool's youngest player to register his maiden goal in the Champions League and second-youngest scorer in the competition after Trent Alexander-Arnold.

But Liverpool's Turkish troubles continued -- they lost twice to Galatasaray last season -- on a typically fractious night in Istanbul, with former Manchester United forward Mason Greenwood scoring the first equalizer with a free kick that deflected in off Jérémy Jacquet.

They had been in total command up to that point but from there the game descended into something more manic, which suited a team hammered 6-0 at Villa Park last month and stoked a febrile home crowd.

Many of Liverpool's players did not cope well in that atmosphere but, to his immense credit, Nyoni shone.

Iraola's choice to leave out Isak, Florian Wirtz and Cody Gakpo as they come to the end of a run of nine games in 27 days was understandable but it left his side toothless.

Bradley Barcola was deployed as striker but his unfamiliarity with the role was evident after failing to properly anticipate Joe Gomez's low cross to the near post. He did flick one header wide but struggled with the physicality of Fenerbahce's center backs, even though Kojo Oppong was making his first Champions League start.

There was a lot of naivety within the visitors' ranks -- Víctor Muñoz snatched at an early chance when he was found in acres of space before redeeming himself by eventually forcing Éderson into a save -- but none of it came from Nyoni.

The teenager was composed on just his seventh Champions League appearance -- with everything going through him at the base of midfield. His use of the ball, tactical awareness and unshakeable belief in his own ability meant he was head and shoulders above everyone else.

Even the usually unflappable Virgil van Dijk's patience was tested, pushing Irfan Kahveci to the floor at a second-half corner, having twice had Romelu Lukaku leave something on him in the early stages.

articles.body:
The NBA is only a few games deep, but leaguewide buzz never stops. 

The LeBron James and Jaylen Brown era with the Philadelphia 76ers got off to an ideal start by spoiling ring night for the New York Knicks. The Detroit Pistons also returned to their regular-season dominance with a win over the Boston Celtics, and the Oklahoma City Thunder struck the first rivalry blow against the San Antonio Spurs this season.

Now, what will Giannis Antetokounmpo's first season away from Milwaukee look like? And how will the other new faces in new places make their impact this season?

All season, bookmark this page for the latest news and reactions from our ESPN NBA insiders.
